I’ve had good experiences at Food Square Worli in the past — the staff is usually polite and the product selection is great.

However, my recent visit left me quite disappointed and feeling cheated. While browsing, I accidentally stepped back and a truffle salt bottle (1500rs) that was placed right at the edge of a shelf fell and broke. Staff and customers nearby agreed it wasn’t my fault. I requested a review of the CCTV footage, but was told the store manager wasn’t available.

Despite that, I was asked to pay 100% first and then settled on 50% of the product’s cost and was given a broken, partially empty container (which on request they changed to a coffee plastic cup)— which I now can’t even use safely due to concerns about glass shards.

This could have been handled more fairly. I hope the store reviews its shelf arrangements and customer service protocols for such incidents.

Freshpik at Jio World Drive, BKC is more than a grocery store — it’s an experiential gourmet food superstore that brings together luxury, convenience, and discovery under one roof.  ￼

🛒 Specialties & Ambience
•	The store is designed to be immersive, blending digital and physical elements, theatrical product displays, and intuitive shopping experiences.  ￼
•	It features kiosks and themed zones — for instance, Cadbury Purple Room (3D chocolate printing), M&M’s Paradise (customize your mixes), and a Wine Library / tasting room for global wine selections.  ￼
•	For cheese lovers, there’s a House of Cheese counter with ~27 types including Brie, Gouda, Danish Blue, Cream Cheese, etc.  ￼
•	The Coffee Studio section caters to coffee aficionados with specialty brews.  ￼
•	Other zones include Tea Garden, ice teas, shakes, Epigamia yogurt bar, fresh salads and counter-made sandwiches.  ￼

📦 Brands & Product Range

•	You’ll find Godiva, Smoor, Cadbury among chocolate / confectionery brands.  ￼
•	Their grocery range covers exotic & organic fruits & vegetables, staples and ingredients for international cuisines (Italian, Korean, Japanese, Thai), healthy / gluten-/sugar-free lines, cold-press oils, dry fruits & nuts, natural & personal care products.  ￼
•	They also stock kitchen accessories, serveware, and gifting options.  ￼

🍃 What Makes It Stand Out
•	The blend of luxury, convenience & entertainment — it’s not just shopping, it’s an experience.  ￼
•	Strong focus on discovery — zones you might not see in a regular supermarket.  ￼
•	Good for foodies, gift shoppers, and people who like premium & imported goods.
•	It’s Reliance’s first foray into ultra-premium grocery, and currently their flagship location.

featured_reviews.name: Kartikeya Pathak
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Luxurious Grocery Experience with a Few Missteps: Freshpik Review

I recently had the opportunity to visit Freshpik, a high-end grocery supermarket located in Jio World Drive. As a foodie, I was excited to explore the aisles and discover some unique and exotic ingredients. Overall, I was impressed with the selection and quality of products, but there were a few missteps that prevented me from giving it a perfect score.

High-End Imported Goods Galore

Freshpik truly lives up to its promise of offering a wide range of high-end imported goods. From artisanal cheeses to gourmet chocolates, the selection is impressive and caters to a discerning crowd. I was particularly excited to find some hard-to-find ingredients, such as truffle oil and infused vinegars.

Well-Organized and Clean Store

The store itself is well-organized and clean, making it easy to navigate and find what you're looking for. The staff is friendly and helpful, although I did find that they could benefit from a bit more product knowledge.

The Cadbury Shake: A Disappointment

Unfortunately, my experience was marred by a lackluster Cadbury shake. I was excited to try this indulgent treat, but it fell flat. The shake was too thin and lacked the rich, creamy texture I've come to expect from a high-end grocery store.

Verdict

Despite the disappointing Cadbury shake, I would still highly recommend Freshpik to anyone looking for a luxurious grocery experience. The selection of high-end imported goods is impressive, and the store itself is well-organized and clean.

featured_reviews.review_text:
(1) I recently attended two weekend food workshops at Nature’s Basket in Phoenix Palladium Mall. The sessions featured four beautifully crafted recipes: Pear–Walnut Crostini with Goat Cheese, Spiced Pear & Almond Galettes, Prune Clafoutis with Spiced Prune Sauce, and Prune Thumbprint Cookies. She welcomed questions with genuine interest and even addressed my broader culinary queries. Her calm and composed teaching style made the entire experience particularly enjoyable. She was ably supported by Chef Mandar and Chef Payal, who assisted her seamlessly during both workshops. (3) The workshop coordinator, Monalita, also deserves special recognition. Her warm personality and efficient handling of participants contributed significantly to the smooth running of the sessions. (4) The workshops are conducted in a dedicated room, equipped with a main kitchen platform for the chef and six island stations for participants. It is rare to find such a thoughtfully designed space for cooking workshops within a gourmet grocery store. (5) Nature’s Basket has long been a shopper’s delight. Its pleasant ambience, courteous staff, and high-quality products make it an ideal destination for all kitchen needs. The store’s wide selection of exotic ingredients is particularly appealing for food enthusiasts. (6) A practical note for visitors: the store is located on the third floor in the West Zone of the mall, useful information, as the East Zone is completely separated from it.

featured_reviews.review_text:

It has all the other sister chains like Fashion at Big Bazar (fbb), Food Bazar et cetera also here. You can find everything that you will need for your house and yourself under one roof here, from home decor, electronic appliances, furniture, toys, cosmetics, groceries to kitchen utensils. Also, everything is well managed and maintained. However, one thing that I find they can improve is to have more support staff who can guide customers. I would also advice them to keep chairs or sofas or make some sort of sitting arrangement in every section or department, because this store is really huge, one really gets tired if you check out every department, especially if you are with kids and elderly. Just a thought. I was also satisfied with the discounts that were on offer. At the same time, if they can up the discounts and offers in their kitchen utensils section that would be great.
Overall it really is a happening place to come shop at. If get hungry or thirsty while shopping, refreshments are also available, you will have to pay for them though..
